blocks.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם אֱלֹהֵי יִצְחָק וֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב הָאֵל הַגָּדוֹל הַגִּבּוֹר וְהַנּוֹרָא אֵל עֶלְיוֹן גּוֹמֵל חֲסָדִים טוֹבִים וְקֹנֵה הַכֹּל וְזוֹכֵר חַסְדֵי אָבוֹת וּמֵבִיא גּוֹאֵל לִבְנֵי בְנֵיהֶם לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ בְּאַהֲבָה.
uncertainties: I can't see a dagesh clearly in the ג of גּוֹמֵל or of גּוֹאֵל. I followed what the print seems to show, but please check against the primary reading.
בְנֵיהֶם: no dagesh is visible in the ב.
וְקֹנֵה is printed defective, with no vav. The holam is on the ק.
The verse ends with a full stop ('.'), not a sof pasuq.

blocks.text: מִסּוֹד חֲכָמִים וּנְבוֹנִים. וּמִלֶּמֶד דַּעַת מְבִינִים. אֶפְתְּחָה פִּי בִּתְפִלָּה וּבְתַחֲנוּנִים. לְחַלּוֹת וּלְחַנֵּן פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים וַאֲדוֹנֵי הָאֲדוֹנִים:
uncertainties: The colon is printed after the closing parenthesis of the conditional variant, which I record as a separate block.
This is a printed alternative ending in smaller unpointed type, placed in parentheses after הָאֲדוֹנִים. The first abbreviation looks like כ״א but could possibly be י״א. ממ״ה = מלך מלכי המלכים.
Its position in reading order is between הָאֲדוֹנִים and the final colon.
Small type. The first letter looks broken (ק-like) but reads as ס.
Centred note above the piyyut, meaning על סדר א״ב (alphabetical acrostic).
Small siglum before אֵת, presumably קהל (congregation).

blocks.text: אֵת חִיל יוֹם פְּקֻדָּה. בְּאֵימָיו כָּל לֶחֶם לְשָׁקְדָה. גָּשִׁים בּוֹ בֶּרֶךְ לְקוֹדָה. דֵּעִם לְיַשֵּׁר כְּעַל מוֹקְדָה: הַיּוֹצֵר יַחַד כֶּסֶל נִשְׁפָּט. וְשׁוֹעַ וָדַל בְּפִלּוּס יִשָּׁפֵט. זֹכֵר לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה מִשְׁפָּט. חִין עֶרְכּוֹ יִזָּכֵר בַּמִּשְׁפָּט: טֶרֶם כָּל מִפְעַל חָצַב. יָזַם בְּמַחֲשֶׁבֶת צוּר חֻצָּב. כְּאָחוֹר וָקֶדֶם כַּתָּוֶךְ
uncertainties: Stanza 1 (א–ד) ends at מוֹקְדָה:, stanza 2 (ה–ח) ends at בַּמִּשְׁפָּט:, and stanza 3 (ט–כ…) continues on the next scan.
לֶחֶם: the mark under ל could be segol or sheva (לְחֶם). The ink is ambiguous.
לְשָׁקְדָה: the mark under ק looks like sheva, but it is faint.
לְקוֹדָה: the vowel under ל is faint. I read sheva, though hiriq is possible, and I see no dagesh in the ק.
דֵּעִם: the vowel under ע could be hiriq or qamats.
וָדַל: the mark under ד looks like patah rather than qamats.
חֻצָּב: the vowel under צ could be qamats or patah, as in the preceding חָצַב.
כַּתָּוֶךְ: the dots at the final kaf are read as the sheva of ךְ, not a stanza colon. The stanza continues on the next page.
There is a small hook or mark below the line near צוּר / חֻצָּב. It is probably a print artefact, not a vowel.

blocks.text: Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God and God of our fathers, God of Abraham, God of Isaac and God of Jacob, great, mighty and awe-inspiring God, God the Most High, who performs acts of kindness and owns everything and remembers the good deeds of the fathers and will bring a redeemer for their children's children for His Name's sake in love.

Choosing from the counsel of wise and discerning men and from the teaching of those that understand knowledge, I open my mouth in prayer and supplication to entreat and implore the countenance of the King of Kings and the Lord of Lords.
uncertainties: The English has no equivalent of the Hebrew parenthetical variant. That absence is left as printed.

blocks.text: The fearful day of reckoning has arrived. All flesh is full of dread of reprimand. They approach to bend the knee before Him, to purify their thoughts as in the flame of the altar. He who has formed the heart of all of them together, judges so that rich and poor alike are judged according to the scales. He remembers him who said: ‘Will He not do justice?’ His valued prayer will be recalled in judgment. Before He formed any creature, he had planned that rock from which we were hewn (Abraham). Central between past and future
uncertainties: The text continues on the next scan.
The quotation marks are curly single quotes.
'he had planned' has a lowercase h in the print, even though 'He' just before it is capitalised. That is kept literal.
